text:
Jonas Brodin is having a quiet season in the box score, eight assists in 25 games and no goals, and that has never been the point of him. Evolving-Hockey had him 17th among 215 defensemen last season and in the 99th percentile at taking chances away, which is about as good as defense gets in their model.

This season is more ordinary. Minnesota is about even on five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), four points worse than without him, and the Wild have scored about 3.6 fewer goals than their chances with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags the weakness: only 28% of his exits keep possession. Now his role grows. With Quinn Hughes out, Brock Faber moved in beside him and played more than 29 minutes in the first game. He has played 940 games, all for the Wild. The next few weeks will lean on him.
